strap: A daily dispatch from the world you are entering

lead.title: Only 2.36 per cent of nannies will work a rotation, and the families who move the most are the ones who cannot fill the post
lead.standfirst: The scarcest people in private service are not the most senior, they are the ones willing to live out of a suitcase.
lead.body:
Morgan & Mallet has published its Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26, drawn from a database of more than 50,300 candidates and from placements made across the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe and the Middle East between January 2024 and October 2025. Buried in the childcare section is a figure that explains why certain posts stay open for months while others fill in a fortnight. Only 2.36 per cent of the nannies on the agency's books will work a rotational schedule, and only 4.82 per cent will travel regularly. Every other candidate is looking for one house, one city and one set of school runs.

Scarcity of that order has a price, and the Gulf pays it. The United Arab Emirates now compensates travelling nannies more generously than any other market in the world, from AED 300,000 to AED 600,000, which the agency converts to as much as USD 163,200 a year. The United States follows at up to USD 150,000, the United Kingdom at up to USD 145,200 and Switzerland at up to USD 132,022. Morgan & Mallet expects Gulf pay for the role to reach USD 180,000 to USD 190,000. Set against a nanny who stays put in France, where the range tops out near USD 67,200, the premium is not being paid for childcare. It is being paid for a strong passport, an unencumbered diary and a willingness to be on an aircraft on Thursday.

The travelling brief is also a short one. Rotational placements typically run from 6 to 12 months before converting into a permanent governess post or a hybrid role, which means the family is back in the market inside a year. The candidates who thrive treat mobility as a documented competence rather than an accident of circumstance: 82 per cent of the agency's Los Angeles candidates for travelling work list domestic and international travel, private aviation included, as an explicit part of their offer.

Underneath the childcare numbers sits a structural change that reaches every role in the house. Average service in a private household has fallen from roughly twenty years to roughly three. Families still working to the old assumption that a post takes 2 to 3 months to fill are now advised to allow 4 to 6. Given that ultra-high-net-worth families commonly keep three to five homes, and that most estate managers run at least three properties at once, the rotation problem is not really a childcare problem. It is the shape of the modern household, and it is arriving at every door in the service wing.
lead.why: The best paid roles in private service are the ones that ask a candidate to be mobile. Rotation experience, travel documents and private aviation familiarity are assets that can be built deliberately, and they now separate a shortlist from a placement.
lead.src: Morgan & Mallet, Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26

articles.title: European business jet flying falls for the first time in fourteen months, while the rest of the world keeps climbing
articles.body:
Argus International's July traffic figures, reported on 11 August, put global business aviation flight activity 5.6 per cent above the same month last year. The headline conceals a split. Europe recorded a decline of 1.2 per cent against July 2025, its first annual contraction in fourteen months, while North America powered the global increase, with turboprops leading the surge there.

The European weakness is concentrated at the top of the market. Large cabin flights across Europe fell 6.5 per cent year on year. That is precisely the tier that carries a principal and an entourage between London, Geneva, Nice and the Gulf without a technical stop, and it is the tier a household is most likely to be arranging on a family's behalf in August. Smaller aircraft held their ground more comfortably.

A single month is not a trend, and July 2025 was an unusually strong comparison. But the direction matters for anyone who books aircraft. When large cabin demand in Europe softens, availability improves and repositioning becomes easier to negotiate late, which is the opposite of the picture in North America, where activity is still climbing and short notice lift remains hard to secure.
articles.why: Anyone who arranges private lift for a family is negotiating against the traffic curve. Knowing which cabin class is loosening in which region is the difference between accepting the first quotation and asking for a better one.

articles.title: Riyadh acquires an ultra-prime address built around large plots, gated enclaves and staff quarters
articles.body:
Wadi Safar, a low density residential district inside the Diriyah masterplan roughly twenty kilometres west of central Riyadh, has emerged as the Saudi capital's first genuinely ultra-prime address. Diriyah is the heritage site recognised as the birthplace of the first Saudi state, and the district around it is being developed as a private estate community with championship golf, five star hospitality and residential plots sized for mansions rather than villas.

Four distinct offerings have been launched within the district: Rayana Mansions, Trump Mansions at Rayana, Altara Diriyah Wadi Safar and Amara Diriyah Wadi Safar. Rayana Mansions is marketed as trophy housing inside a gated enclave, aimed at Saudi families, Gulf investors and international buyers, and is designed explicitly for multi-generational living, with privacy, staff accommodation and entertaining space named as the organising principles. Altara sells land to buyers who intend to commission their own house. Amara offers a dual mansion format, two separate residences on a single large plot, for extended families or for guests who need full residential function rather than a spare room.

The supply model is deliberately restrictive: large plots, gated enclaves, controlled release, a pattern borrowed from Emirates Hills and the Palm Jumeirah villa communities in Dubai, where scarcity of land rather than volume of construction did the work of establishing prestige. Riyadh's own demand base is domestic before it is international. Saudi family offices and high-net-worth individuals form the core of the buyer pool, supplemented by Gulf and international capital, while the regional headquarters programme has pushed a new layer of executive housing demand into the city.

For the private service reader, the significant detail is not the golf course. It is that staff accommodation and entertaining capacity are being designed into these houses at the plan stage rather than retrofitted, and that the dual mansion format implies two households under one ownership, with guest wings that operate independently. Houses of that shape do not run on two people. They run on a structured team with written protocol, and they are being built now.
articles.why: A new ultra-prime district is a new employment market. Houses designed from the outset around staff quarters, guest wings and multi-generational occupancy require larger teams and clearer lines of authority than the villa stock they are replacing.

articles.title: The London art season opens in a public park in September and peaks in The Regent's Park in October
articles.body:
Frieze London and Frieze Masters return to The Regent's Park from 14 to 18 October, running side by side across a single site, one fair devoted to contemporary work and the other spanning several millennia of art history. This year's curated sections carry 50 presentations, given over to young galleries and to artists showing in London for the first time, which is where dealers and advisers look first for the names that will move in price before the winter sales.

The season in fact opens a month earlier and costs nothing to attend. Frieze Sculpture occupies the English Gardens of The Regent's Park from 16 September to 1 November, free and outdoors, with eleven international artists including Angel Otero, Conrad Shawcross, Tarini Sethi and Ivana Basic. It runs for six and a half weeks, which makes it one of the few fixtures in the London cultural calendar a household can build into a visiting principal's diary without a ticket, an invitation or a queue.

October in London is a week when the private diary compresses. Principals fly in for the fairs and stay for the auctions that cluster around them, houses fill with guests, private views and dinners land on consecutive evenings, and a car is needed in Regent's Park at hours when Regent's Park is difficult. The dates are published in June for a reason. The households that read them in August are the ones that are not improvising in October.
articles.why: Cultural fluency in private service is practical before it is decorative. Knowing when the fairs open, what is free and what requires an invitation is how a house manager anticipates a principal's autumn rather than reacting to it.

briefs.b: The Monaco Yacht Show holds its 35th edition in Port Hercule from 23 to 26 September, with a fleet expected to reach 120 yachts by opening day, 43 of them delivered during 2026. The organisers note that build slots at leading yards are now committed through 2028 and 2029, which makes a hull delivering this year one of the scarcer commodities in the market.

Demand for private chefs is concentrated in five markets. The United States accounts for 35 per cent of global requests, the United Arab Emirates and the wider Middle East for 20 per cent, France and Monaco for 20 per cent, Switzerland for 15 per cent and the United Kingdom for 10 per cent. In Los Angeles, 41 per cent of placed chefs hold certification in nutrition alongside their culinary qualification.
briefs.src: Morgan & Mallet, Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26

briefs.b: In France, 21 per cent of the agency's clients over the past year asked for a domestic couple and could not find one, making it the most persistently unfilled brief in that market. In the United States, estate manager requests account for 10 per cent of the total, and half of all estate manager posts worldwide sit in American households.
briefs.src: Morgan & Mallet, Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26

briefs.t: USD 18 trillion of it to charity
briefs.b: Of the USD 124 trillion expected to change hands in the United States through 2048, USD 105 trillion goes to heirs and USD 18 trillion goes to charity. More than half of the total, USD 62 trillion, comes from high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth households, who make up only 2 per cent of all households.
